Olivia — appreciate the concrete asks. High level answers up front:

- Planned failover RTO (full session routing + KV reconverge) under Dedicated: 3–7 minutes typical, SLA target 15 minutes for activation.
- Expected user-visible latency uplift after failover to eu-west-1 (US traffic): median +120ms, p95 +250ms depending on client routing.
- KV cache RPO: our standard cross-region replication provides asynchronous kv-prefix replication with an operational RPO target of 30s; legal-facing contractual RPO is 60s for Dedicated (we document any longer windows as exceptions).

I'm attaching a short table and a diff of the runbook that highlights the fallback path we expect to rely on when cross-region warm-standby is used. There are two important caveats to call out:

1) If BrightBank elects to use our preemptible extension in the standby region to lower costs, RTO/RPO variance increases (RPO up to 5 minutes, RTO up to 30 minutes in worst-case).
2) Under extreme cascading outages where control plane reachability is compromised, we have an additional manual activation path that will increase activation time; we prefer to keep that as an operational fallback, not standard SLA.

Next steps: I propose a short table you can include in the amendment and two optional carve-ins we discussed (1. cost-optimized standby with looser guarantees, 2. guaranteed warm standby with the 60s RPO commitment). Let me know which BrightBank prefers and I'll route to legal.

Olivia — quick technical clarifications inline: 

> 1) does the 60s RPO include in-flight KV entries that haven't hit object store?

Short answer: Yes, the 60s contractual RPO for strict warm standby refers to the full end-to-end application-facing state that we consider durable for customer workloads. For clarity we break state into two buckets:
- ephemeral session/cache entries (KV) that are replicated asynchronously but are considered part of the RPO calculation; under strict warm standby we hold a journal for those keys and guarantee replication commitment within 30s in normal conditions.
- canonical persisted writes to object store (S3-equivalent) which are independent and fall under our standard storage durability SLA.

If replication is delayed beyond thresholds (network partition or preemptible eviction), our detection and alerting will trigger early notification and we have a rollback checklist in the runbook that includes: 
- immediate traffic rebalancing to origin
- KV namespace reconciliation task
- rolling re-provision of warm standby nodes

> 2) latency dataset

We ran a controlled synthetic test using 50k concurrent simulated US clients from three pop locations (SFO, ORD, NYC) hitting a mirrored traffic shape and measured egress to eu-west-1 with our edge routing policy. I'll attach the script and the raw CSVs. The synthetic profile and scripts are the same ones we use for our perf benchmarks. They show median +110–130ms and p95 ~240–270ms depending on test day (network jitter).

Next steps on our side: I'll ask Legal to treat the 30s contractual RPO as an optional addendum (option B) with the understanding BrightBank will accept the increased reserved capacity price. We'll prepare the annotated amendment and the DocuSign link after we confirm the checklist. Expect a DocuSign draft by EOD tomorrow.

Olivia — confirming next steps and adding the activation verification checklist you requested. Draft checklist (short form) we will include in the amendment and in the runbook annex: 

1) Pre-activation sanity: health checks green for control-plane, KV sync status <= 30s, no active provisioning alerts.
2) Canary traffic shift: 5% of traffic for 1 minute; monitor error rate, latency drift, auth token validation.
3) Full cutover: progressive increase to 100% over 3 minutes if canary metrics are within thresholds.
4) Post-activation reconciliation: KV namespace diff job, warmed caches seeded within 60s, read-repair run for partial keys.
5) Rollback trigger: if client error rate increases >1.5x baseline OR p95 latency exceeds agreed threshold for >2 minutes, automatically revert traffic to origin and open incident with both teams.

We'll attach the full annotated runbook and the minimal legal amendment with the exact phrasing for 30s RPO under option B. I'm sending a DocuSign link for the amendment now: https://app.docusign.com/BB-DR-AMENDMENT-1783 (also included in related_links).
